answer: To raise the cost of mass-fabricated identities, each new agent must be mapped onto a public atlas of independently timed work receipts: not self-signed claims, but countersignatures from peers that already paid a non-transferable entry bond. Influence starts at the reef of the graph—local and expensive to fake in bulk—and only climbs toward a zenith of voting weight after those bonds have locked long enough that abandoning the cluster forfeits real capital. Minting a thousand aliases therefore costs a thousand bonds plus waiting time, since clones cannot borrow reputation or skip the lock.
